children: Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has quashed more than a decade-old tax proceedings against Israeli drugmaker Teva Pharmaceutical Industries and its US affiliate arising from a deal with Ranbaxy Laboratories, and reprimanded tax authorities for withholding a 783 crore refund for more than 10 years.

In the absence of any provision for protective tax recovery under the I-T Act, 1961, the department's decision to withhold Teva Pharmaceutical's refund for assessment years 2012-13 to 2014-15 for more than 10 years was "utterly arbitrary, to the extent of being confiscatory", a division bench of justices Dinesh Mehta and Vinod Kumar said.

The court directed the department to refund the entire 783 crore, comprising tax deducted at source, along with interest within two months. Ranbaxy Laboratories had deducted TDS from payments made to Teva Pharmaceutical Industries.

The tax dispute arose from agreements between entities of the Ranbaxy and Teva groups concerning the commercial exploitation of Atorvastatin, the generic version of Pfizer's cholesterol-lowering drug Lipitor, in the US. Quashing the tax notices issued to Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, the court said the income tax department cannot withhold Teva Pharmaceutical Industries' refund on the ground that proceedings had been initiated against Teva Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. Proceedings against the US entity under Section 148 had also been stayed by the court, it said.

The court said if no action on alleged tax evasion had been taken by US authorities, authorities in India cannot take action because the authorities of US and Israel chose not to impose tax or have chosen not to exercise their right. The right to tax is not a right of exclusion but a right of exaction-a right conferred by statute, the judges said, adding that unless the statute and Constitution confer such right, tax authorities couldn't impose tax simply because some income had not suffered tax under any country's I-T laws.

title: HC Orders 783cr Tax Refund with Interest to Teva
